name: Accumulation
definition: Piling up words or clauses that restate a point.
example: He was a rogue, a cheat, a thief, a liar.'
effect: Builds weight and momentum until the point feels inescapable.

name: Adynaton
definition: Hyperbole so extreme it names an impossibility.
effect: Dismisses something as never going to happen.

name: Allegory
definition: A whole narrative that stands for something else.
example: Animal Farm as the Russian Revolution.
effect: Lets a writer attack a real target under cover of a story.

name: Alliteration
definition: Repeated initial consonant sounds in nearby words.
effect: Binds words together and slows the reader onto them.

name: Allusion
definition: A passing reference to another text, person or event.
effect: Borrows the weight of the thing referred to without explaining it.

name: Amblysia
definition: Softening language placed before bad news.
example: I am afraid there is no easy way to say this.'
effect: Prepares the listener and softens the blow.

name: Amphiboly
definition: Ambiguity caused by grammar rather than word choice.
effect: Creates doubt or a joke from structure alone.

name: Anachronism
definition: Something placed outside its proper time.
example: A clock striking in Julius Caesar.
effect: Jolts the reader, or draws a deliberate line to the present.

name: Anacoluthon
definition: A sentence that breaks off and restarts in a new grammar.
example: I warned him that if he — but he never listened.'
effect: Mimics a mind losing its thread; agitation or interruption.

name: Anadiplosis
definition: Ending a clause with the word that begins the next.
example: Fear leads to anger; anger leads to hate.'
effect: Chains ideas into a chain of consequence.

name: Analogy
definition: An extended comparison used to explain.
example: Comparing the heart to a pump.
effect: Makes the unfamiliar graspable through the familiar.

name: Anaphora
definition: Repeating the same words at the start of successive clauses.
example: We shall fight on the beaches, we shall fight…'
effect: Drums a point in and builds rhythm.

name: Anastrophe
definition: Inverted word order.
effect: Throws stress onto the displaced word; can sound archaic or grand.

name: Anecdote
definition: A short personal story used as evidence.
example: A speaker opening with a memory of their grandmother.
effect: Makes an argument feel lived rather than abstract.

name: Anesis
definition: A final clause that undercuts everything before it.
example: He was rich, admired, adored — and utterly alone.'
effect: Deflates or complicates the build-up.

name: Antagonist
definition: The force or figure opposing the protagonist.
effect: Gives the protagonist something to be measured against.

name: Antanaclasis
definition: Repeating a word in a different sense.
example: Put out the light, and then put out the light.'
effect: Turns a phrase on itself; wit or grim irony.

name: Anthimeria
definition: Using one part of speech as another.
effect: Fresh, compressed, often energetic.

name: Anthropomorphism
definition: Giving an animal or object full human form and behaviour.
example: Talking, clothed animals in a fable.
effect: Lets a writer say human things through non-human figures.

name: Anthypophora
definition: Asking a question and immediately answering it.
example: What should we do? We should act.'
effect: Controls the argument by voicing and closing the objection.

name: Antimetabole
definition: Repeating a phrase with the order reversed.
example: Ask not what your country can do for you…'
effect: Balanced and memorable; makes a claim sound proven.

name: Antiphrasis
definition: One word used to mean its opposite.
effect: Ironic, often affectionate or mocking.

name: Antithesis
definition: Contrasting ideas balanced in parallel structure.
example: It was the best of times, it was the worst of times.'
effect: Sharpens both halves by collision.

name: Antonomasia
definition: A title or epithet used in place of a name.
effect: Elevates, or reduces a person to one quality.

name: Aphorism
definition: A short, pointed statement of a general truth.
effect: Sounds settled and quotable; closes debate.

name: Aposiopesis
definition: Breaking off mid-sentence, unfinished.
example: If you ever do that again —'
effect: The unsaid threat or feeling is stronger than the said.

name: Apostrophe
definition: Addressing someone absent, dead, or an abstraction.
example: O Death, where is thy sting?'
effect: Raises the emotional register; makes the absent present.

name: Archaism
definition: Deliberately old-fashioned language.
effect: Signals age, authority, or distance from the present.

name: Archetype
definition: A recurring character type or pattern.
effect: Lets a reader recognise a role instantly.

name: Aside
definition: A line spoken to the audience, unheard by others on stage.
effect: Creates complicity; the audience knows more than the characters.

name: Assonance
definition: Repeated vowel sounds in nearby words.
effect: Links words musically; slows or smooths a line.

name: Asyndeton
definition: Omitting conjunctions between items.
example: I came, I saw, I conquered.'
effect: Speeds the line and makes it feel clipped and decisive.

name: Bathos
definition: A sudden drop from the lofty to the trivial.
example: He lost his wife, his home, and his umbrella.'
effect: Comic deflation, or a sign the speaker has no sense of proportion.

name: Bildungsroman
definition: A novel tracking a character from youth to maturity.
effect: Frames the whole book as the making of a person.

name: Black comedy
definition: Humour drawn from grim or taboo subjects.
effect: Makes horror bearable and sharper at once.

name: Blank verse
definition: Unrhymed iambic pentameter.
effect: Close to natural speech while keeping formal weight.

name: Blazon
definition: A catalogue of a lover's features, part by part.
effect: Praises by inventory; can read as dismantling the person.

name: Bombast
definition: Inflated language out of proportion to its subject.
example: A speech of grand words about nothing.
effect: Exposes a speaker as pompous or hollow.

name: Burlesque
definition: Treating a serious subject trivially, or a trivial one grandly.
example: A mock-epic about a card game.
effect: Mockery by mismatch of style and subject.

name: Cacophony
definition: Harsh, clashing sounds.
example: the crack, jag and grate of it'
effect: Makes the reading uncomfortable; matches violence or disorder.

name: Caesura
definition: A pause within a line of verse.
example: To err is human || to forgive, divine.'
effect: Breaks the rhythm; forces a beat of thought.

name: Call to action
definition: A direct instruction to the audience to do something.
effect: Turns agreement into behaviour; usually placed last.

name: Catachresis
definition: A strained or mixed metaphor.
example: to take arms against a sea of troubles'
effect: Strains sense to convey extremity of feeling.

name: Catalexis
definition: A metrical line missing its final unstressed syllable.
effect: Ends the line abruptly; insistent, drum-like.

name: Catharsis
definition: The purging of pity and fear through tragedy.
effect: The audience is released rather than merely upset.

name: Chekhov's gun
definition: A detail planted early that must matter later.
example: A pistol shown in act one.
effect: Nothing is idle; rereading rewards the reader.

name: Chiasmus
definition: Ideas repeated in reverse order (ABBA).
example: Never let a fool kiss you or a kiss fool you.'
effect: Balanced, closed, satisfying; feels like proof.

name: Circumlocution
definition: Talking around a thing rather than naming it.
effect: Evasion, politeness, or padding — usually revealing.

name: Cliché
definition: A phrase worn out by overuse.
example: at the end of the day'
effect: Usually a fault; deliberate use can characterise a speaker.

name: Colloquialism
definition: Informal, everyday language.
effect: Creates closeness, or places a speaker socially.

name: Conceit
definition: An extended, ingenious and unlikely comparison.
effect: Shows off the mind making the link; sustains a whole poem.

name: Connotation
definition: The associations a word carries beyond its literal sense.
effect: Where most close analysis actually happens.

name: Consonance
definition: Repeated consonant sounds, not only at the start.
effect: Knits a line together; often harsher than assonance.

name: Couplet
definition: Two consecutive rhyming lines.
example: The final two lines of a Shakespearean sonnet.
effect: Snaps a poem shut; feels conclusive.

name: Cyclical structure
definition: A text ending where it began.
example: A novel closing on its opening image.
effect: Suggests inescapability, or change measured against sameness.

name: Defamiliarisation
definition: Making the ordinary strange so it is seen again.
example: Describing a horse as if never seen before.
effect: Forces attention onto what habit has made invisible.

name: Denotation
definition: A word's literal dictionary meaning.
effect: The baseline connotation is measured against.

name: Deus ex machina
definition: An unearned outside force resolving the plot.
effect: Usually a flaw; occasionally a deliberate comment on chance.

name: Dialect
definition: Regional vocabulary and grammar.
effect: Places a speaker; can carry the writer's sympathies.

name: Direct address
definition: Speaking straight to the reader as 'you'.
effect: Closes the gap; makes the reader complicit or accused.

name: Dissonance
definition: Deliberately jarring, unharmonious sound.
example: Clashing consonants in a war poem.
effect: Unsettles the ear to match unsettling content.

name: Double entendre
definition: A phrase open to two readings, one usually indecent.
effect: Wit, and a way to say what cannot be said openly.

name: Dramatic irony
definition: The audience knows what a character does not.
effect: Turns every line into something else; builds dread.

name: Dysphemism
definition: A harsh term used where a neutral one exists.
effect: Aggression, contempt, or bleak humour.

name: Ecphonema
definition: An exclamation of emotion.
effect: Marks the point where feeling breaks through.

name: Ekphrasis
definition: A vivid description of a work of art.
effect: Lets one art form interrogate another.

name: Elegy
definition: A poem of mourning.
effect: Frames the whole poem as an act of grief.

name: Elision
definition: Omitting a sound or syllable to fit the metre.
effect: Keeps the beat; signals a formal metrical scheme.

name: Ellipsis
definition: Omitted words, or the mark showing omission.
example: I went to the shop; she, to the park.'
effect: Compresses, or leaves a gap the reader fills.

name: Emotive language
definition: Words chosen to provoke feeling.
effect: Moves the audience before they have reasoned.

name: Enjambment
definition: A sentence running over the line break without pause.
effect: Pulls the reader on; sense and line pull against each other.

name: Epanados
definition: Repeating an idea in reverse order to expand on each part.
example: She loved him, and he her — she for his wit, he for her calm.'
effect: Unpacks a pair without losing the balance.

name: Epanalepsis
definition: Beginning and ending a clause with the same word.
effect: Encloses the thought; feels sealed and circular.

name: Epexegesis
definition: Added words that clarify what came before.
example: He fled — ran, rather, without looking back.'
effect: Corrects and sharpens in the same breath.

name: Epideictic oratory
definition: Speech of praise or blame, for an occasion.
effect: Its job is to affirm shared values, not to decide anything.

name: Epigraph
definition: A quotation placed at the head of a text.
example: A poem opening a novel's chapter.
effect: Frames everything that follows before it begins.

name: Epistrophe
definition: Repeating the same words at the end of successive clauses.
example: …of the people, by the people, for the people.'
effect: Hammers the final word home.

name: Epitasis
definition: The part of a play where the action intensifies.
example: The middle acts of a tragedy.
effect: Names the rising action as a structural stage.

name: Epizeuxis
definition: Immediate repetition of a word, no words between.
effect: Raw insistence; feeling outrunning argument.

name: Euphemism
definition: A mild term standing in for a harsh one.
effect: Softens, evades, or exposes a speaker's discomfort.

name: Euphony
definition: Pleasant, smooth-sounding language.
example: season of mists and mellow fruitfulness'
effect: Makes the line pleasurable; matches calm or beauty.

name: Farce
definition: Comedy built on improbable situations and mistaken identity.
effect: Speed and absurdity over character.

name: Feminine rhyme
definition: A rhyme on two syllables, the last unstressed.
effect: Softer, falling ending; often comic or tender.

name: Flashback
definition: A scene set earlier than the main action.
effect: Supplies cause after effect; reframes what we have seen.

name: Flyting
definition: A formal exchange of insults.
effect: Conflict fought with words as a display of skill.

name: Foil
definition: A character whose contrast lights up another.
effect: Shows what the protagonist is by showing what they are not.

name: Foreshadowing
definition: An early hint of what is to come.
effect: Builds dread; makes the ending feel inevitable rather than arbitrary.

name: Frame narrative
definition: A story told inside another story.
example: Wuthering Heights through Lockwood and Nelly.
effect: Puts distance between reader and events; raises the question of who is telling.

name: Free verse
definition: Verse without regular metre or rhyme.
effect: Freedom from pattern; shape must be made by other means.

name: Hamartia
definition: The flaw or error that brings a tragic figure down.
effect: Makes the fall the character's own rather than bad luck.

name: Hemistich
definition: Half a line of verse, often broken by a pause.
effect: Fragments the line; interruption or exhaustion.

name: Hendiadys
definition: One idea expressed as two nouns joined by 'and'.
example: sound and fury' for furious sound.
effect: Splits an idea to slow it down and weight both halves.

name: Homonym
definition: Same spelling and sound, different meaning.
example: bat' the animal and the bat you swing.
effect: The engine of most puns.

name: Homophone
definition: Same sound, different spelling and meaning.
effect: Wordplay, and a common source of deliberate ambiguity.

name: Hubris
definition: Overreaching pride that invites downfall.
effect: Names the fault the tragedy will punish.

name: Hypallage
definition: An adjective attached to the wrong noun.
effect: Displaces the feeling onto the object; dreamlike.

name: Hyperbaton
definition: Words separated from their normal partners.
effect: Stress falls where the disruption is.

name: Hyperbole
definition: Deliberate exaggeration.
example: I have told you a million times.'
effect: Intensity, or comedy at the speaker's expense.

name: Hypocorism
definition: A pet name or diminutive.
effect: Affection, condescension, or infantilising.

name: Hypostatisation
definition: Treating an abstraction as a real thing.
effect: Hides who is actually doing the demanding.

name: Hypotyposis
definition: Description so vivid the scene seems present.
example: A battle described as if watched.
effect: Collapses the distance between reader and event.

name: Hypozeuxis
definition: Every clause given its own verb and subject.
example: He came. She saw. They left.'
effect: Weighty and deliberate; each clause stands alone.

name: Idiom
definition: A phrase whose meaning is not its literal parts.
effect: Marks a speech community; opaque to outsiders.

name: Imagery
definition: Language appealing to the senses.
effect: The umbrella term — always name the sense and the type.

name: In medias res
definition: Beginning in the middle of the action.
effect: Throws the reader in; back-story must be recovered later.

name: Invective
definition: Violent denunciation.
effect: Anger given full rein; character revealed by its excess.

name: Inversion
definition: Reversing normal word order.
effect: Stresses the fronted word; can sound poetic or archaic.

name: Invocation
definition: A formal appeal to a muse or deity at the outset.
effect: Signals epic ambition and asks for authority.

name: Irony
definition: Saying one thing and meaning another.
effect: Opens a gap between what is said and what is meant.

name: Isocolon
definition: Clauses of equal length and matching structure.
effect: Balance and control; sounds authoritative.

name: Jargon
definition: Specialist vocabulary of a trade or group.
effect: Includes insiders and shuts out everyone else.

name: Juxtaposition
definition: Placing two things side by side for contrast.
example: A wedding scene beside a funeral.
effect: The meaning is made by the join, not by either part.

name: Kenning
definition: A compound metaphorical name.
effect: Compresses a metaphor into a noun; marks Old English verse.

name: Light rhyme
definition: A rhyme pairing a stressed with an unstressed syllable.
effect: Unsettles the expected chime; slightly off-balance.

name: Litotes
definition: Understatement by denying the opposite.
effect: English understatement; can be modest or withering.

name: Malapropism
definition: The wrong word used for a similar-sounding one.
effect: Comic; exposes pretension.

name: Masculine rhyme
definition: A rhyme on a single stressed final syllable.
effect: Firm, closing; the standard English rhyme.

name: Meiosis
definition: Belittling something by understatement.
effect: Diminishes; can be evasive or bitterly ironic.

name: Melodrama
definition: Exaggerated emotion and sensational plot.
effect: Feeling over plausibility; sometimes knowingly used.

name: Metalepsis
definition: Crossing a boundary between narrative levels.
effect: Breaks the frame; exposes the fiction as made.

name: Metaphor
definition: Saying one thing is another.
example: He is a lion in battle.'
effect: Transfers the qualities of one thing onto another outright.

name: Metonymy
definition: Naming a thing by something closely associated.
effect: Shifts attention onto the chosen association.

name: Metre
definition: The regular rhythmic pattern of a line.
effect: The beat the poem sets and can then break.
notes: Listed as 'Meter' — UK spelling is metre.

name: Microcosm
definition: A small world standing for a larger one.
effect: Lets a whole system be examined at a manageable scale.

name: Monologue
definition: One character speaking at length.
effect: Gives one voice the floor; the others cannot answer.

name: Motif
definition: A recurring image, idea or object.
effect: Accumulates meaning by repetition across the whole text.

name: Mythopoeia
definition: The making of an original mythology.
effect: Builds a world with its own depth of past.

name: Neologism
definition: A newly coined word.
effect: Names something the language had no word for.

name: Nonce-word
definition: A word coined for one occasion only.
effect: Sound carries the sense where meaning cannot.

name: Onomatopoeia
definition: A word imitating the sound it names.
effect: Puts the sound in the reader's mouth.

name: Oxymoron
definition: Two contradictory words placed together.
effect: Holds a contradiction the speaker cannot resolve.

name: Palilogy
definition: Repetition of a word for emphasis.
effect: Insistence, or emptiness through repetition.

name: Paradox
definition: A statement that contradicts itself yet holds a truth.
example: I must be cruel to be kind.'
effect: Forces the reader to reconcile two things.

name: Paralipsis
definition: Raising something by saying you will not mention it.
effect: Says the thing while disowning having said it.

name: Parallelism
definition: Matching grammatical structures across clauses.
effect: Rhythm and balance; implies the parts are equivalent.

name: Parataxis
definition: Clauses placed side by side without subordination.
example: I came home. It was dark. I slept.'
effect: Flat, unhierarchical; often numb or childlike.

name: Parenthesis
definition: An interruption inserted into a sentence.
example: The house — his father's — was sold.'
effect: A second voice or afterthought inside the main one.

name: Paronomasia
definition: A pun — wordplay on similar sound, different meaning.
example: Not on thy sole, but on thy soul, thou art a cobbler.'
effect: Wit; forces two meanings into one word.

name: Pathetic fallacy
definition: Nature reflecting human feeling.
effect: Makes the world complicit in the mood.

name: Pathos
definition: An appeal to the audience's emotion.
effect: One of the three rhetorical appeals with ethos and logos.

name: Periphrasis
definition: Using many words where few would do.
effect: Padding, evasion, or ceremony.

name: Personification
definition: Giving human qualities to something non-human.
effect: Animates the inanimate; invites sympathy.

name: Platitude
definition: A flat, obvious remark offered as wisdom.
effect: Fills a silence without saying anything.

name: Plosive
definition: Hard stopped consonants: p, b, t, d, k, g.
effect: Percussive and abrupt; anger or violence.

name: Polyptoton
definition: Repeating a root word in different forms.
example: Judge not, that ye be not judged.'
effect: Turns a word over to show its different faces.

name: Polysyndeton
definition: Repeated conjunctions between items.
example: and the rain and the wind and the dark'
effect: Slows and accumulates; overwhelming or relentless.

name: Prodiorthosis
definition: A warning that what follows may shock.
effect: Prepares the audience and heightens what comes.

name: Prolepsis
definition: A flash-forward, or answering an objection early.
example: You will say I am biased.'
effect: Controls the future of the argument or the plot.

name: Protagonist
definition: The central figure whose choices drive the story.
effect: The reader's route into the world.

name: Refrain
definition: A repeated line or phrase across stanzas.
effect: Returns the poem to one idea; incantatory.

name: Repartee
definition: Quick, witty reply.
effect: Displays intelligence and equality between speakers.

name: Rhetorical question
definition: A question asked without expecting an answer.
effect: Makes the reader supply the conclusion themselves.

name: Rhyme
definition: Matching sounds at line ends.
effect: Binds lines; a broken pattern is where meaning often sits.

name: Rhythm
definition: The pattern of stress in a line.
effect: Carries pace and mood beneath the sense.

name: Satire
definition: Using ridicule to expose a fault.
effect: Attacks by making the target absurd.

name: Semantic field
definition: A group of words sharing a subject area.
example: Words of war throughout a love poem.
effect: Shows the writer's underlying frame of thought.

name: Sentence structure
definition: The build of a sentence: simple, compound, complex, minor.
example: A run of short sentences after a long one.
effect: Pace, emphasis and control of the reader's breath.

name: Setting
definition: Where and when a text takes place.
effect: Shapes what is possible and mirrors the interior.

name: Sibilance
definition: Repeated s, sh and z sounds.
example: the soft hiss of the sea'
effect: Hushed, sinister or soothing depending on context.

name: Simile
definition: Comparing with 'like' or 'as'.
effect: Keeps the two things separate — unlike metaphor.

name: Sonnet
definition: A fourteen-line poem in a set rhyme scheme.
effect: The turn and the form itself carry meaning.

name: Statistics
definition: Numerical evidence used persuasively.
effect: Borrows the authority of measurement.

name: Stichomythia
definition: Rapid alternating single lines of dialogue.
effect: Verbal duelling; conflict at speed.

name: Stream of consciousness
definition: Prose following the unbroken flow of thought.
effect: Interiority without the ordering a narrator would impose.

name: Symbolism
definition: An object standing for an idea.
effect: Carries meaning the text need not state.

name: Synaesthesia
definition: Describing one sense in terms of another.
effect: Fuses sensations; heightened or disordered perception.

name: Syncope
definition: Omitting a sound from the middle of a word.
effect: Keeps the metre; compresses speech.

name: Synecdoche
definition: A part standing for the whole, or the whole for a part.
effect: Reduces people to their function, or expands one detail.

name: Tapinosis
definition: Demeaning language that belittles its subject.
effect: Undercuts dignity; contempt.

name: Theme
definition: A central idea a text explores.
effect: What the text is about beneath what happens.

name: Tmesis
definition: Splitting a word by inserting another.
effect: Emphasis through disruption; colloquial force.

name: Tone
definition: The attitude a text takes to its subject.
effect: The reader's guide to how to take everything else.

name: Topothesia
definition: Description of an imaginary place.
effect: Builds a place that argues a case.

name: Tricolon
definition: Three parallel items in a row.
effect: Three feels complete; the most durable rhetorical shape.

name: Unreliable narrator
definition: A narrator whose account cannot be trusted.
example: The governess in The Turn of the Screw.
effect: Forces the reader to read against the telling.

name: Verisimilitude
definition: The appearance of being true to life.
effect: Buys the reader's belief so the rest can be risked.

name: Voice
definition: The distinctive personality of the writing.
effect: What makes a text sound like itself and no other.

name: Volta
definition: The turn in a sonnet where the argument shifts.
effect: The structural hinge — where the poem changes its mind.

name: Zeugma
definition: One verb governing two objects, often oddly.
example: She took her coat and her leave.'
effect: Wit through the yoking of unlike things.

name: Zoomorphism
definition: Giving animal qualities to a person or thing.
effect: Reduces the human to instinct.
